stem:
Kabir knows a common calendar year has $365$ days and Earth's revolution is about $365.2422$ days.

Which two claims correctly reason about leap-day adjustments?

options.text: Earth revolution is the calendar rule's name, so divisibility need not be checked.
The extra about $0.2422$ day accumulates, so about every $4$ years an extra day is added.
Under the usual rules, a year divisible by $4$ is a leap year, with century-year exceptions.
A year is a leap year when the digits of the year look symmetric.

teacher.key_rationale: The 0.2422-day gap accumulates to about one day every four years, and divisibility rules (by 4, with century exceptions) assign leap days. Renaming the topic "Earth revolution" skips those rules. Symmetric-looking digits are a surface feature.
